## Intent
Hypothesis: a branchless blend with per-particle hash RNG can vectorize across particle components and approach the streaming ceiling, with death rate only modestly raising the floor.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, cost drops from 7.076 ns/p at N=10000 (past L1d spill at 963, within L2) to 5.875 at N=100000 (past L2 spill at 61680), then flat at 5.798–5.864 through N=10M. The L2→DRAM spill produces no knee — cost falls slightly, indicating overhead amortization. At q=0.1 the curve is flat at 6.83–6.97; q=0.25 flat at 8.35–8.55; q=0.5 flat at 10.93–11.07. Death rate raises the floor (5.8→6.8→8.4→11.0 ns/p) without altering the N-shape.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 11.73 GB/s at N=1M, q=0.01 — 39% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.1: 9.89 GB/s (33%); q=0.25: 7.96 GB/s (27%); q=0.5: 6.15 GB/s (21%). The algo is compute-bound: 80% compute at q=0.01, N=1M. The transition is by death rate — branch_flush rises from 4.7% (q=0.01) to 45.1% (q=0.5), shifting the bottleneck from compute to branch overhead. Bandwidth never approaches the ceiling.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across components of one particle, not across particles: `fmul.4s v18, v21, v2` and `fadd.4s v18, v19, v18` operate on four float lanes within a single 68-byte struct; `ext.16b v21, v19, v20, #0xc` and `mov.s v21[3], v18[0]` rearrange components. A single `ld1.s {v20}[1], [x24]` is an indexed gather. The scatter phase uses 17 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` — byte-granular accesses that cannot stream. Eighteen `csel` implement branchless selection, but 20 `b` plus `cbz`, `tbnz`, `ccmp` remain, explaining the branch_flush cost. Component-wise vec on stride-68 explains 39% of ceiling; byte-granular scatter caps it further.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 the algo sustains only 11.73 GB/s = 39% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling with 80% compute, confirming compute-bound behavior. Hash RNG dominates cost, and branch_flush rises from 4.7% to 45.1% as death rate goes from 0.01 to 0.5, collapsing throughput to 6.15 GB/s = 21% of ceiling. The byte-granular scatter (`strb` ×17) prevents streaming in every regime.
